correctness.rationale: The strong Roman definition gives an exact excess requirement \(\lceil(z-z_i)/2ceil\) for a defender in part \(V_i\). A zero-free defender part yields the target lower bound; if all defender parts contain zeros, two such parts are forced and the presence of a third part yields an even stronger bound. The explicit smallest-part labeling attains \(\lceil(N+m)/2ceil\). Exhaustive direct-definition verification through order \(10\) found no smaller labeling.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Total strong Roman domination imposes an additional condition on the positive support, so its complete-multipartite results do not imply ordinary strong Roman domination. The later k-strong Roman work treats a different generalization and emphasizes complete bipartite cases, not the original invariant on arbitrary multipartite graphs with at least three parts.

value.rationale: The result is a natural exact classification of a standard domination invariant on all complete multipartite graphs with at least three parts. It identifies a whole equality class for a classical upper bound, supplies an explicit optimum, and explains why the two-part boundary behaves differently.
